uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of the displayed physical scale.
additionalSystematics: Usui2011§2.3 explicitly omits unquantified shape/spin/thermal-model effects; rotation can add a few to about10%in size, especially for fewdetections. No invented numerical confidence interval is assigned to these unquantified effects.
diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Its use as the volume-equivalent diameter of the separate convex DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published physical-volume calibration.
limitations: The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. Both 2013 convex poles (90,14) and (269,15) remain plausible. Model 557 is a representative solution; neither a smaller model ID nor the ordering in the paper establishes a preferred pole. Use the original unscaled coordinates with an explicitly approximate AKARI thermal-size scale.
visibleDescription: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 108.41 km (catalog ±1.67 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size is used as a volume-scale approximation. An alternative pole remains possible. The grid marks unavailable imagery.
